superseded: MERGED AND NO LONGER READ BY ANYTHING. All 38 pairs below were folded into namefold.json, which is what /register/, /searched/ and /people/ actually import; checked on 20 September 2026 and all 38 are present there with the same targets, so the search behaves correctly. THIS FILE IS KEPT FOR ITS REASONING, NOT ITS DATA — the note and the `why` block below are the argument for hand-written folds, and the measurement that made the case. DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE EXPECTING THE SITE TO CHANGE: edit namefold.json.
note: WRITTEN, NOT DERIVED — the half of the fold map no rule can find. namefold.py clusters spellings of one word: Booijsen with Booyzen, Coetsee with Coetzee. It cannot know that JOHANNES and JOHN are the same name, because they share almost no letters; that is a fact about Afrikaans and English, not about these records. Measured in this archive's own register, eleven such doublets account for 8,931 occurrences of which the English form is 1,783 — so a reader searching JOHN BOOYZEN was seeing a fifth of what is here. FOLDING IS A SEARCH RULE AND NOTHING ELSE: it widens what a query matches and never merges a record, a person or a line.

why.montjoy: Not an orthographic rule but this archive's own reading: JAMES MONTJOY the saddler, d. Cradock 1827, is the father of the twenty-seven MOUNTJOYs here, and the spelling changed at the Cape rather than the family. 383 tokens against 10,730. Recorded here rather than in the derived clusters because it is a judgement about a family, and a rule that reached it would also reach names that are not related at all.
why.bynames: DELIBERATELY ABSENT. Catherine Maria Sophia “Kathleen” Barry is findable under Kathleen already, because the byname is inside her name. Folding a nickname into a language form would put three different things — a translation, a nickname and a clerk's error — into one bucket, and telling them apart is the whole point of the catalogue this estate has yet to build.
why.jan: REMOVED, AND IT TOOK A BROWSER TO SEE IT. JAN is a real given name in this family and it is also how every date on this site writes January. Folded to JOHANNES it made 338 of the 346 people match a search for JOHN, because almost everybody has a January somewhere in their dates. Word-by-word folding cannot tell a name from a month, so the name loses: searching JAN no longer reaches JOHANNES here, which costs one spelling and saves the page from answering every query with everything. It was measured in the page, not reasoned about - the map looked entirely sensible on paper.
why.johannesburg: A SIDE EFFECT, MEASURED RATHER THAN GUESSED AT. The filter matches substrings on purpose, so that ZUBRIN finds Zubrinic; that means JOHANNES has always also matched JOHANNESBURG, and folding JOHN to JOHANNES hands JOHN the same 18 rows. On /people/ that is 18 of 346, and every one of them was already reached by searching JOHANNES. Word-boundary matching would end it and would also stop a partial spelling finding anything, which is the behaviour the box is built around. Recorded here because a known 18 is worth more than a clean-looking map.
